readmeHtml:
xtool

Cross-platform Xcode replacement. Build and deploy iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

Overview

xtool is a cross-platform (Linux/WSL/macOS) tool that replicates Xcode functionality with open standards.

✅ Build a SwiftPM package into an iOS app

✅ Sign and install iOS apps

✅ Interact with Apple Developer Services programmatically

Getting Started

  1. Follow the guide to install xtool
    • Installation (Linux/Windows)
    • Installation (macOS)
  2. Create and run your first xtool-powered app by following the tutorial!

Examples

Screenshot

Command line interface

$ xtool --help
OVERVIEW: Cross-platform Xcode replacement

USAGE: xtool <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

CONFIGURATION SUBCOMMANDS:
  setup                   Set up xtool for iOS development
  auth                    Manage Apple Developer Services authentication
  sdk                     Manage the Darwin Swift SDK

DEVELOPMENT SUBCOMMANDS:
  new                     Create a new xtool SwiftPM project
  dev                     Build and run an xtool SwiftPM project
  ds                      Interact with Apple Developer Services

DEVICE SUBCOMMANDS:
  devices                 List devices
  install                 Install an ipa file to your device
  uninstall               Uninstall an installed app
  launch                  Launch an installed app

  See 'xtool help <subcommand>' for detailed help.

Library

You can consume xtool itself as a Swift Package, to enable your own app to interact with Apple Developer Services, iOS devices, and more. You can use this by adding XKit or XToolSupport as a SwiftPM dependency.

Note: while we aim to uphold semver semantics on the CLI interface (breaking change = major version bump), the Swift interface does not offer the same guarantees.

// package dependency:
.package(url: "https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool", .upToNextMinor(from: "1.2.0"))
// target dependency:
.product(name: "XKit", package: "xtool")
readmeExcerpt:
# xtool

Cross-platform Xcode replacement. Build and deploy iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, and macOS.

## Overview

xtool is a cross-platform (Linux/WSL/macOS) tool that replicates Xcode functionality with open standards.

✅ Build a SwiftPM package into an iOS app

✅ Sign and install iOS apps

✅ Interact with Apple Developer Services programmatically

## Getting Started

1. Follow the guide to install `xtool`
    - [Installation (Linux/Windows)](https://xtool.sh/documentation/xtooldocs/installation-linux)
    - [Installation (macOS)](https://xtool.sh/documentation/xtooldocs/installation-macos)
2. Create and run your first xtool-powered app by following the [tutorial](https://xtool.sh/tutorials/xtooldocs/first-app)!

## Examples

### Screenshot



### Command line interface

```bash
$ xtool --help
OVERVIEW: Cross-platform Xcode replacement

USAGE: xtool <subcommand>

OPTIONS:
  -h, --help              Show help information.

CONFIGURATION SUBCOMMANDS:
  setup                   Set up xtool for iOS development
  auth                    Manage Apple Developer Services authentication
  sdk                     Manage the Darwin Swift SDK

DEVELOPMENT SUBCOMMANDS:
  new                     Create a new xtool SwiftPM project
  dev                     Build and run an xtool SwiftPM project
  ds                      Interact with Apple Developer Services

DEVICE SUBCOMMANDS:
  devices                 List devices
  install                 Install an ipa file to your device
  uninstall               Uninstall an installed app
  launch                  Launch an installed app

  See 'xtool help <subcommand>' for detailed help.
```

### Library

You can consume xtool itself as a Swift Package, to enable your own app to interact with Apple Developer Services, iOS devices, and more. You can use this by adding `XKit` or `XToolSupport` as a SwiftPM dependency.

Note: while we aim to uphold semver semantics on the CLI interface (breaking change = major version bump), the Swift interface does not offer the same guarantees.

```swift
// package dependency:
.package(url: "https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool", .upToNextMinor(from: "1.2.0"))
// target dependency:
.product(name: "XKit", package: "xtool")
```

releases.name: v1.22.2
releases.body:
## Breaking Changes

This release updates the device fingerprint used for Apple ID-based login (we now present to Apple as a Pixel 7 device), fixing auth issues.

If you use Apple ID auth, you'll need to log in again after updating.

## What's Changed
* planner: skip macro targets by @pawlowskialex in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/208
* packer: use XcodeProjectFormat for generate-xcode-project by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/300
* packer: custom SwiftVersion parser by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/303
* gsa: fix login using mismatched client-info by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/337
* http: add newer Apple Root CAs by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/340

## New Contributors
* @pawlowskialex made their first contribution in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/208

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/compare/1.21.0...1.22.2

releases.name: v1.21.0
releases.body:
## Breaking Changes

**Darwin hosts:** the deployment target for xtool is now macOS 14.0 / iOS 17.0. This shouldn't matter to CLI users because Swift 6-compatible toolchains require macOS 14.5+ anyway, but may be relevant to consumers of the XKit/XToolSupport libraries.

## What's Changed

* sdk: get clang resources from swift toolchain by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/274 (fixes https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/issues/273)
* deps: bump deps by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/271, https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/278, https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/281, https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/298
* build: compile xtool with Swift 6.4 by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/272
* package: bump Darwin deployment targets to Fall2023 by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/277
* sdk: prune Xcode when installing from xip by @kabiroberai in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/280
* tests: derive CFBundleSupportedPlatforms from the build triple by @mvanhorn in https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/pull/289

releases.body:
## What's Changed

* Adds support for FoundationModels macros (#270)
* Fixes `ld64.lld` erroring out with "unknown architecture: arm64e.x1-ios" when linking apps built using Xcode 27 (#270)
* Fixes failure to find `dsymutil` when building for release on Swift 6.4 (#270)


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/xtool-org/xtool/compare/1.20.0...1.20.1

aiSummary.oneLiner: Cross-platform Xcode replacement to build, sign, and deploy iOS apps with SwiftPM on Linux, Windows, and macOS.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: xtool replicates core Xcode functionality using open standards across multiple operating systems. It enables building SwiftPM packages directly into iOS applications on Linux, WSL, and macOS environments. The tool also handles the signing and installation of iOS apps to physical devices or simulators. Furthermore, it allows programmatic interaction with Apple Developer Services for tasks like authentication and SDK management. By decoupling iOS development from Xcode and macOS, it provides a flexible toolchain for developers.
keyFeatures: Cross-platform compilation: Build SwiftPM packages into iOS apps on Linux, Windows (WSL), and macOS.
App signing and deployment: Sign iOS applications and install them directly to connected devices.
Apple Developer Services integration: Programmatically authenticate and interact with Apple Developer Services.
SDK management: Manage and utilize the Darwin Swift SDK for cross-compilation.
Device management: List, install, uninstall, and launch applications on target iOS devices.
Swift library: Integrate xtool's functionality directly into Swift applications using the XKit package.

useCases.title: Develop iOS apps on Linux/Windows
useCases.description: Create and build iOS applications without requiring a physical Mac or macOS virtual machine by leveraging SwiftPM and the Darwin Swift SDK.

useCases.title: Automate CI/CD pipelines
useCases.description: Run automated builds, signing, and deployments for iOS apps on standard Linux CI runners, reducing dependency on expensive macOS instances.

useCases.title: Programmatic Apple Developer interaction
useCases.description: Use the built-in commands or XKit library to authenticate and script interactions with Apple Developer Services.

useCases.title: Cross-platform tooling
useCases.description: Build custom development tools or IDE integrations for iOS development that work across different operating systems.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: iOS developers seeking to write and build apps on non-macOS platforms like Linux or Windows. It is also highly useful for DevOps engineers automating iOS builds on Linux-based CI/CD infrastructure.
